- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment peaks recently.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0 point unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price by 0.5–1.5 points when sentiment is weak or mixed; add 0.3–0.7 point upward adjustment.
